LESSON: FABRIC DECORATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.2: Fabric Decoration
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fabric Decoration, part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is fabric decoration important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fabric Decoration together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: a learner develops the skill of connecting with technology as they use digital devices with appropriate

assistive technology to explore virtual and actual sources to study techniques of fabric decoration

• Creativity and imagination: a learner develop the skills of flexibility as they decorate the fabric using applique technique

Values:
• Love: a learner demonstrates the skills humility as they portray a caring attitude while working together in decorate a fabric

using tie and dye techniques

• Responsibility: a learner demonstrates the skills of safety as they handles tools for decorating fabrics by trimming and

ironing with care.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Social cohesion: a learner develops the skills of appreciation as they talk about their own and others' work in a just manner.

• environmental conservation :a learner develops the skills of conserving environment as they sources materials such as

recyclable fabrics, tying/stitching/pasting

Link to other learning areas:

Agriculture and nutrition: as learners studies techniques of fabric decoration focusing on; tie and dye, applique and materials in

fabric decoration.
